evidence: Several internal navigations use a raw HTML `<a href="/...">` anchor with an unprefixed absolute path instead of the app's locale-aware `Link` from `@/i18n/routing`. The i18n router is configured `localePrefix: 'as-needed'` (src/i18n/routing.ts:8), so non-default locales carry a prefix (/de/listings, /cs/listings) while sk (default) does not. A bare `<a href="/listings">` therefore always resolves to the NO-PREFIX = default-locale (sk) route, so a de/cs/en visitor who clicks it is dropped out of their language mid-session (and gets a full document reload, losing client state).

ListingDetailContent.tsx:145 `<a href="/">` and :147 `<a href="/listings">` are the breadcrumb on the PUBLIC, SEO-indexed listing detail page (the highest-traffic entry point); ListingDetailContent.tsx:38 `<a href="/listings">` is the not-found back-link. auth-button.tsx:158 `<a href="/favorites">` and :162 `<a href="/profile">` are in the global header account menu shown on every page. CsvImport.tsx:996 `<a href="/agency/listings">` is the post-import 'view listings' action.

This is DISTINCT from the already-logged `code-review-reality-web-auth-nav-drops-locale` (2026-09-05), which covers programmatic `router.push`/`router.replace` imported from `next/navigation` in the three auth PAGES (register/reset-password/login) — a different mechanism in different files. The anchor case here was not previously flagged. Confidence medium: the locale-drop is inferred from the documented `as-needed` config + the app's own convention (sell/page.tsx and the rest of the app use `Link` from `@/i18n/routing`, which sell/page.tsx:17-22 explicitly documents as required to keep a SK user on /sk/terms), not runtime-confirmed. Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): replace each plain `<a href>` internal link with `import { Link } from '@/i18n/routing'`; no backend/DB work.

A cluster of date renders call `new Date(...).toLocaleString()` / `.toLocaleDateString()` with NO locale argument and no timeZone. In a Next.js SSR app this formats on the Node server with the server's default locale/timezone during SSR, then re-formats in the browser with the visitor's locale/timezone on hydration — a classic React hydration-mismatch source — and either way ignores the active next-intl locale, so a cs/de/en visitor sees dates in the server/browser default format rather than their chosen app language.

SyncSchedule.tsx:232 `new Date(schedule.nextRunAt).toLocaleString()` and :526 `new Date(item.startedAt).toLocaleString()`; FeedImport.tsx:207 `new Date(feed.lastFetchAt).toLocaleDateString()` and :263 `new Date(item.startedAt).toLocaleString()`; CrmConnection.tsx:196 `new Date(connection.lastSyncAt).toLocaleString()` and :202 `new Date(connection.nextSyncAt).toLocaleString()`; AgencyListings.tsx:406 `new Date(listing.updatedAt).toLocaleDateString()`; AdditionalInfo.tsx:42 `new Date(listing.availableFrom).toLocaleDateString()` and :48 `new Date(listing.createdAt).toLocaleDateString()`.

Net-new: the prior `code-review-reality-web-categorycards-tolocalestring-no-locale` (2026-09-07) is a NUMBER count on CategoryCards, and the en-US price findings (listingheader/agencylistings/additionalinfo -en-us-price) are explicit-`'en-US'` price formats — both different from these no-arg DATE calls (AdditionalInfo's date lines are separate from its already-flagged price line). Severity low (i18n/UX + potential hydration warning; no data/auth impact). Confidence medium (static read; default-locale landing + hydration behaviour inferred from Next.js/Intl semantics). Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): pass the active next-intl locale (via `useLocale()` / `useFormatter()`) or a shared date formatter with an explicit timeZone; no backend/DB work.

auth-button.tsx — the global header auth control (sign-in button + logged-in account dropdown, rendered on every page via the shared Header) — has ZERO next-intl usage (no `useTranslations` import, no `t(` call in the file) and ships its user-facing strings hardcoded in English: 'Sign In' (:127), 'My Favorites' (:159), 'Profile' (:162), 'Sign Out' (:165). A sk/cs/de visitor sees an English account menu on every page, which contradicts the app's i18n convention (all user-facing copy comes from `messages/<locale>.json`).

Net-new: auth-button.tsx is not referenced in any prior reality-web signal; the earlier i18n-gap findings target realtor/account/import/comparison/listing-grid surfaces, not this shared header component. Severity low (i18n gap, no data/auth impact; high visibility because it is global). Confidence medium (static read confirms the literals and the absence of any translation call). Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): add `useTranslations` and move the four strings into `messages/<locale>.json`; no backend/DB work.
